metas.name: Switzerland  - Barns - Ticino Huts
metas.note: Huts in Ticino often have stone as their primary building material, with their roofs often made from slate tiles.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland  - Roof Features - Low-Pitched Roofs
metas.note: Wide houses with strikingly low-pitched roofs and often a large number of windows are frequently found in the cantons of Jura and Neuchâtel, as well as in the northern part of the canton of Bern. A variant with a half-hipped roof also exists.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Attached Barns
metas.note: Barns in Appenzell and the surrounding area are often directly attached to the main house in a T-shaped or L-shaped layout, making them often easy to recognise from a distance.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Barn Lofts
metas.note: These upper-floor wooden balconies are commonly seen on barns in southwestern Valais.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Bulky Barns
metas.note:
In the canton of Bern, the design of barns generally mirrors the local architecture. Barns in this region are typically bulky in appearance and frequently have half-hipped roofs. The roofs may also feature timber supports.

A variant exists with an additional entrance for vehicle access. Sometimes the barn will be directly attached to the house.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Corner Barns
metas.note: Barns featuring a combination of wood and either concrete or stone can be found in Valais and Grisons. Typically, the concrete or stone elements are located at the corners of the barns. As with huts, exposed round beams are only found in Grisons.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Cyborg House-Barns
metas.note: In the Entlebuch region, in the far south of the canton of Lucerne, you can find ‘cyborg’ house-barns with the house and barn ‘fused’ together. These buildings are particularly striking when viewed from the front.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Flap-Roof Barns
metas.note: Like houses in the same region, barns in the area shown on the map can sometimes have double-pitched gable roofs, with the lower part of the roof at a shallower angle.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Grisons Huts
metas.note: A key feature of huts in Grisons is the frequent use of round beams, rather than rectangular ones, either for the overall structure or just in the gable area. Huts with just rectangular beams can still be seen in this area.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Low-Pitched Roofs
metas.note:
Barns in the cantons of Jura and Neuchâtel often have low-pitched roofs, mirroring the design of local houses.

The barns often form part of the same building as the main house, although can be separate. Either version may feature large double doors for vehicle access.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Raccards
metas.note: Raccards are the traditional raised wooden granaries of Valais. They are generally built on short stilts with a round stone slab on each stilt to guard against rodents.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Tent-Roof Barns
metas.note: Strikingly wide barns with tent-like roofs, resembling those found on houses in the region, can be found in the northern half of the canton of Bern.A variant of these barns exists with an additional covered entrance allowing vehicle access.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Tiled-Gable Barns
metas.note:
In western Fribourg, you can find barns with gables that are clad with either terracotta-coloured tiles or occasionally grey, diamond-shaped ones.

A variant of these barns also exists with an additional entrance for vehicle access.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Traverse Roof Barns
metas.note: In **Zug **and neighbouring cantons, you can find barns with a prominent transverse roof extending below the main gable.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Undulating Gable Arches
metas.note:
Similar to houses in the region, barns in the canton of Lucerne can feature an undulating gable arch, or, unlike the houses, a semicircular gable arch.

Barns in this area may also have a distinctive style of half-hipped roof with a tiny triangular gable.

Variants of these barns exist with an entrance for vehicle access.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - Valais Huts
metas.note: The walls of wooden huts in Valais are often made from a system of interlocking rectangular logs, easily visible from the outside of the building.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Barns - X-Barns
metas.note: This diamond lattice pattern on the doors of barns is found in the cantons of Thurgau and Zurich.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Churches - Multi-Spire Churches
metas.note: Church towers featuring multiple small spires surrounding a main spire are most common in the west of the country, particularly around Neuchâtel, although they can occasionally be seen elsewhere
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Churches - Multi-Triangle Gable Churches
metas.note: Church towers where the tower walls form triangular gables, pointing up, on multiple sides, occur most frequently in the northeast.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Churches - Onion-Dome Churches
metas.note: Churches with onion domes are a strong indicator for the non-French-speaking regions of Switzerland, although exceptions exist elsewhere.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Churches - Onion-Shaped Clock Churches
metas.note: Church towers featuring an onion-shaped gable structure around a clock face can be found in a central band from the canton of Bern in the west to Glarus in the east.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Churches - Rooster Church Steeples
metas.note: A rooster on top of a church steeple usually signifies a Protestant church and is a strong indicator for the French-speaking part of the country, although isolated examples can be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Churches - Simple Triangular Gable Churches
metas.note: Church towers with a simple triangular gable shape are most frequently found in northern and central Switzerland.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Religious Shrines -Ticino Cappellittas
metas.note: Catholic shrines in Ticino will often be colourful and feature religious imagery. Shrines in this area may also have slate roofs.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Balcony Gables
metas.note: In the canton of Neuchâtel, these wide houses with low-pitched roofs will sometimes have a balcony integrated into the gable. You will also sometimes see wood-clad gable arches on these houses.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Bump Finials
metas.note: Finials in the form of a small bump on a roof can be found in the areas shown on the map, being common in the cantons of Vaud, Fribourg, Geneva and Neuchatel and also in western Valais. They can also very rarely be found in the canton of Bern.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Diamond-Shaped Slates
metas.note: Roofs featuring large, diamond-shaped, slate slabs are found across central Valais.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Downward Pointing Finials
metas.note: Downward-pointing finials at the ends of the load-bearing beams on gable roofs can be found in the areas shown on the map. They can take a variety of shapes, ranging from rectangular to ornamental forms.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Flap Roofs
metas.note: Double-pitched gable roofs, with the lower part of the roof at a shallower angle, can be seen in the area shown on the map.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Front Chimneys
metas.note: Chimneys located on the small gable roof of ​​half-hipped roofs or very close to the gable on hipped roofs are particularly found in western Switzerland, especially in the cantons of Vaud and Fribourg, although exceptions can rarely be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Gable-End Chimneys
metas.note: In the valleys of central Ticino, you will find houses with gable-end chimneys.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Metal Panel Roofs
metas.note: In Valais and Grisons, rectangular metal panels are sometimes used to roof houses and sheds. They are particularly found in the northwest of Grisons.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Slate Roofs
metas.note: Slate roofs are commonly found in the three southern cantons of Valais, Ticino, and Grisons.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Tent Roofs
metas.note: Strikingly wide houses resembling tents, with deeply overhanging roofs and a bulky overall appearance, can be found in the northern half of the canton of Bern.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Thick Arched Gables
metas.note: In the canton of Bern and neighbouring cantons, houses featuring half-hipped roofs with a thick arch under the gable, giving the house a bulky appearance, can be found.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Ticino Slates
metas.note: In Ticino, slate roofs will sometimes be organised in neat rows of slate tiles, as opposed to the less regular pattern normal on other slate-roofed houses in Switzerland.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Tiled House Gables
metas.note: Houses with gables covered with striking red tiles are frequently found in northeastern Vaud and the west of the canton of Fribourg. In exceptional cases, similar tiled gables can be found outside these regions however.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Undulating Gable Arches
metas.note: Gables in the canton of Lucerne commonly have arches similar to those you see in the canton of Bern. However unlike the simple semicircular arches in Bern, the arches are undulating.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Roof Features - Valsot Flat Roofs
metas.note: Most houses in Valsot, in the extreme east of the country, have very flat roofs with a barely noticeable slope. These houses can also be found in other nearby villages.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Arched Gates
metas.note: Houses with arched gates can be found in the north and west of the country as shown on the map. Traditionally serving as entrances to farmhouses and barns, they now often conceal modern apartments, shops or restaurants.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Colorful Shingle Wall Cladding
metas.note: Shingle walls in a range of pastel colours are found primarily in the east of the country, becoming less common towards the west, although can be occasionally found anywhere. The shape of shingles can vary: round, rectangular, diamond and cone shapes all exist.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Decorative Carvings
metas.note:
Dark-wood houses that are particularly wide can be seen in the southern parts of the cantons of Bern and Vaud and in northwestern Valais.

Common features of these houses include:

  • wood carvings and inscriptions with the year of construction or other text
  • decorative soffits can along the edge of the roof
  • either a staircase or a pair of staircases
  • covered balconies and verandas on the side of the house.

You can also see timber versions of the thick arched roofs common in this area.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Devant Huis
metas.note: A devant-huis is a traditional, wide, recessed entranceway of a building found in the canton of Jura. There will often be vertical timber plank cladding above the entrance.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Light Colored Mortar
metas.note: Buildings with walls made of irregular stones plastered with a thick, light-coloured mortar, often smeared over the stones, are found in Valais, Ticino and the Italian-speaking parts of Grisons.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Pale Yellow Bricks
metas.note: Pale yellow bricks are found in a broad strip stretching from Bern in the west to St. Gallen in the east. Buildings can be entirely constructed from these bricks. However, you can also often see the bricks used in conjunction with decorative red bricks and in otherwise wooden buildings.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Rectangular Panel Houses
metas.note:
A very distinctive style of house is found in the Appenzell cantons and neighbouring St. Gallen.

These houses have rows of sets of shutterless windows on the gable side of the house, with rectangular panels underneath and between the sets of windows.

A ‘baroque’ variant of this style can be found, commonly in urban settings, with a distinctive curved roof shape and often decoration on the panels.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Sgraffito
metas.note: In Grisons, you will find the traditional decorative technique known as sgraffito, where intricate patterns or motifs are carved into the fresh, light lime plaster of house facades to reveal the darker layer of plaster beneath.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Sgraffito Val Müstair
metas.note: Val Müstair, in the far east of Grisons, paints its houses with a unique variant of Grisons sgraffito with more colours and a different style of designs. Normal sgraffito can also be found here
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Structural Curve Houses
metas.note: In Obwalden and surrounding areas, you can find dark-wood houses (in varying styles) with a structural curve along the length of a wall supporting a cantilevered upper storey. This upper storey sometimes includes a balcony.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Subtle Window Roofs
metas.note: Houses with ‘miniature roofs' over windows are found in the area shown on the map. Sometimes these ‘miniature roofs' will span the whole wall and sometimes just the windows below them.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Tall & Narrow Houses
metas.note:
Dark-wood houses in the mountainous north-south valleys of Valais are comparatively tall and narrow.

Often roofed with slate tiles, these houses frequently feature multiple balconies and decorative wooden fretwork. Interlocking log joints, a typical feature of the region, are usually visible at the corners of the houses.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Timber & White-Plastered Walls
metas.note: Houses blending timber and white-plastered walls are most common in Valais and northern Grisons, typically following a one-third to two-thirds ratio of either material.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Timber Frame Houses East
metas.note:
Timber frame houses are found in two main regions of Switzerland as shown on the map. There are rare exceptions elsewhere.

In the northeastern distribution area, common features of timber frame houses include double-pitched gable roofs and large dormers. Additionally these houses can sometimes take the form of long buildings running lengthwise along the street.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Timber Frame Houses West
metas.note:
Timber frame houses are found in two main regions of Switzerland as shown on the map. There are rare exceptions elsewhere.

In the western distribution area, you will often see timber frame houses with thick arched gables, triangular timber supports under the roof, and large tent roofs.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Window Roofs
metas.note: Houses featuring multiple small roofs on the gable end can be found in the areas shown on the map, although can exceptionally be found elsewhere. The small roofs will sometimes also continue along the side walls of the building.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerland - Wall Features - Wooden Shingle Wall Cladding
metas.note: Traditional wooden shingle wall cladding is found across a central belt stretching from the canton of St. Gallen in the east to Valais in the west. The shapes of the shingles can vary and may be rounded or angular.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Switzerlans - Roof Features - Slate Finials
metas.note: In the southernmost parts of Valais, notably around Zermatt and Evolène, you can sometimes find slate roofs featuring slate finials above the gables.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Switzerland Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord
